body:
Problem:
Non-primary cursors use shape 29 (follow primary), so they look
identical
to the main cursor instead of using hl-MCursor colors.

Solution:
Detect terminal support for shapes 30/40 (cursor/text color). When
available, send MCursor fg/bg sRGB values via the protocol before
setting cursor positions.

comment_data.body: when would this be false if `tty_cursors` is true? if a terminal supports kitty cursors then we can just assume it supports coloring them, or it can ignore the colors.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -12,6 +12,8 @@ local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace('nvim.multicursor')
 local vcur_ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace('nvim.multicursor.cursor')
 --- Kitty cursors protocol: host terminal supports the protocol.
 local tty_cursors = false
+--- Kitty cursors protocol: host terminal supports cursor coloring (shapes 30, 40).
+local tty_cursor_colors = false

comment_regular_data.body:
Couple of observations:

- I don't think using `MCursor` is the right choice here. It might be a choice for (many) color schemes to make non-Kitty case have more subtle background than Kitty case (since the background color is used for a thin vertical bar cursor). I'd be in favor of creating a dedicated highlight group (for example `MCursorT`, for `Terminal`) that by default links to `MCursor`.
- It is better for changes of the original group to be respected even if the cursors are currently shown. For example, via autocommand for the `ColorScheme` event, like was originally suggested in #41603 and in a more refined [this snippet](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41900#issue-5440841372).
- Those colors should also reset to not affect applications outside of Nvim.
- Nvim highlight groups are more complicated than just setting foreground and background. The main problem here is the presence of `gui=reverse`. If present, it reverts `fg` and `bg`. And if either `fg` and `bg` is missing, it uses the color of the cursor cell. Both of these cases need to (and seem possible to) be accounted for.

Another idea to make a `guicursor` options for extra cursor. Or emit "extra cursor style" in ui event https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d16bd456a8307158181a2aa659e5b78772f98cc5/runtime/doc/api-ui-events.txt#L172-L198... then tui process emit kitty mc protocol and fallback to place "fake block" (not sure if still possible)

> I don't think using `MCursor` is the right choice here.

?? `MCursor` is the multicursor highlight. If users don't want that they can simply unset it.

> > I don't think using `MCursor` is the right choice here.
> 
> ?? `MCursor` is the multicursor highlight. If users don't want that they can simply unset it.

There is "multicursor that is always a whole cell block" (most of the terminal emulators) and there is "multicursor that is sometimes whole cell block and sometimes thin vertical bar highlighted with a background color" (Kitty and maybe handful of others in the future).

It is not unheard of (for color scheme authors and users in general) to want to "whole block cell" be highlighted in not-so-bright color (at least to maybe preserve the foreground highlighting) while the "vertical thin bar" should remain visible with somewhat-bright color. Unfortunately, Kitty multiple cursors protocol supports only a single pair of colors that is used for both "whole block cell" and "vertical thin bar".

Allowing to use different highlight groups for Kitty and non-Kitty cases will open the possibility to have not-so-bright background for at least non-Kitty cases (which, again, is most terminal emulators).

> Allowing to use different highlight groups for Kitty and non-Kitty cases will open the possibility to have not-so-bright background for at least non-Kitty cases

Sounds related to UI-specific options:

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40388
- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40356

and is out of scope here. We can revisit later, it's not blocked by this short-term fix.

> Sounds related to UI-specific options:

It's most certainly not. This is closer to having both `Normal` and `NormalNC`: not strictly necessary, but allows color schemes to provide more customized behavior.

And yes, this in theory can be expanded in the future, but at more cost than introducing and using a new dedicated highlight group right away. Not a really strong opinion, but certainly in a "nice to have" category.

Accounting for [other issues](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41935#issuecomment-5698885728) is more important, though. Especially for the `hi MCursor gui=reverse` and `hi MCursor guifg=#ffffff gui=reverse` cases.

> > Sounds related to UI-specific options:
> 
> It's most certainly not. This is closer to having both `Normal` and `NormalNC`

What name do you suggest?
I don't think this makes anything worse, and it doesn't block the other concerns raised above. So let's try this out.

> > > Sounds related to UI-specific options:
> > 
> > 
> > It's most certainly not. This is closer to having both `Normal` and `NormalNC`
> 
> What name do you suggest?

There was a suggestion [earlier](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41935#issuecomment-5698885728). In general, to follow the `MCursor` + `suffix`. Like `MCursorP` (for `Protocol`), `MCursorK` (for `Kitty`), etc.

> I don't think this makes anything worse, and it doesn't block the other concerns raised above. So let's try this out.

The following cases misbehave exactly as described:

And if either `fg` and `bg` is missing, it uses the color of the cursor cell. Both of these cases need to (and seem possible to) be accounted for.

That is not "worse" than the previous situation.
